archetype: Mardu Vampire typal go-wide aggro that kills by trigger, not by combat. deck-audit matches aggro from strategic_frame.json and every structural axis agrees: 30 creatures inside the 26-32 band, 37 land copies, threat-density 11 against a floor of 3. The frame is right about what this deck is. The sixteen swaps moved it off the aristocrats build the commander is usually given and onto the entry-trigger build, and the artifacts now describe one deck rather than two.
verdict: This is a genuinely good linear deck with one honest bottleneck. The bodies arrive — a lord or anthem lands in 83.2% of games, a token multiplier in 78.2% — and stack 009 verified the plan those bodies feed: one {B}{B} Vampire through one doubler and three payoffs is nine triggers and 12 damage at every seat. What binds is the payoff half. Four cards convert a creature entry into each-opponent damage, they are in hand in 52.5% of games, and the joint go-wide kill — a payoff AND a multiplier — is only 40.2% assembled and 27.5% by turn six. Everything else the deck could spend a slot on is worth less than a fifth converter.

open_questions.question: Does Mirkwood Bats trigger once per token when a single token-creation event is doubled by Anointed Procession, Mondrak or Elspeth — i.e. does one eminence trigger under two doublers cause four life loss at each seat, or one?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the difference between a fifth converter that compounds with the deck's three replacement-effect doublers and a flat one-per-event drip. The whole case for the add rests on which it is, and stacks 002 and 008 already established the doubled-event board this would be resolved on.

open_questions.question: Olivia's Wrath resolving on the deck's own board: is Purphoros a creature for the -X/-X, does killing your own creatures change X or your devotion mid-resolution, and do Cathars' Crusade counters already on Corpse Knight and Mondrak survive it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Five of thirty creatures are non-Vampires — Corpse Knight (a converter), Mondrak (a doubler), Abzan Falconer, Ocelot Pride and Purphoros. Nobody has priced the deck's one-sided sweeper against the deck, and the answer decides whether it stays.

open_questions.question: What does the GO-WIDE KILL rate become with a fifth entry-trigger payoff in the any_of group?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The binding claim in this diagnosis is that the payoff class at 4 gates the primary kill at 27.5% by turn six. Adding the candidate to goldfish_targets.json and re-simulating measures the delta directly instead of inferring it from the hypergeometric.

open_questions.question: Does the Reconnaissance line work as the primer claims — remove attacking Vampires from combat after Edgar's attack trigger and Sanctum Seeker's attack triggers have resolved, keeping the +1/+1 counters and the drain?
open_questions.why_it_matters: deck_recon.json carries it as a one-source claim about this exact shell. If it holds, a one-mana white enchantment converts every attack into a free drain with no combat risk, which is a different kind of add from anything in the list above. Nothing in this repo has verified it.

open_questions.question: Does the corpus support a rule for pricing noncreature-answer DEPTH once breadth is covered, in a linear deck already over its interaction template?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This diagnosis overturns the strategic frame's claim that the 23.8% noncreature-answer rate is what binds, and the argument rests on critical-mass's general line about answer slots rather than on anything measuring the cost of an unanswered anti-token permanent. The frame's own gaps list names the same hole.

gaps: The colour delta of the Brightclimb Pathway swap could not be measured. mana_analysis.json is tracked and this artifact is read-only, so the on-curve rates for the changed base were not computed. Running mana-analysis after the swap would settle it.

goldfish_targets.json declares only entry-triggered conversion. Bontu's Monument (cast trigger), Sanctum Seeker (attack trigger) and Throne of the God-Pharaoh (end step, tapped creatures) also convert width into each-opponent life loss and are in no any_of group, so the measured 52.5% is the rate for the doubler-composing subset, not for conversion as such.
considering.json and tutor_guide.json are stale against this decklist and were deliberately not read or cited.

The synergy graph contributes nothing here: all 33 intra-deck edges are lands pointing at Herald's Horn under one Ramp + Cost Reduction rule, and its pool candidates for this deck are an aura package (All That Glitters, Ethereal Armor, Hyena Umbra) that belongs to a different archetype. deck-facts says why — it is a format-wide top-10 shortlist, not a fit score.

The strategy corpus has no section on token doubling as a multiplicative resource, on converting board width into non-combat damage, or on typal critical mass. This deck's entire plan is those three things, so every axis reading above is borrowed from adjacent sections.

deck_recon.json is dated as_of 2026-08-03 and two of the six adds lean on it. Several of its findings — Command Tower, Cavern of Souls, Charismatic Conqueror, Anguished Unmaking, Warleader's Call, Impact Tremors, Elspeth, Caretaker's Talent, Legion's Landing — have already been applied, so the remaining findings are what is left of a pass that was largely consumed.

No opposing-interaction model exists. Every assembly rate quoted is from a goldfish that simulates resource development with no removal and no sweeper, which is exactly the axis (card-advantage after a wrath) this diagnosis calls the second weakness.
